content:
Dear Verdane Care Hiring Team,

I am applying for the Full-Stack Engineer role on the Patient Experience team. My experience building accessible React interfaces, alongside project-based work with TypeScript, Node.js, Express and PostgreSQL, has prepared me to contribute to patient-facing web features from the frontend through to supporting APIs and data.

During my Software Development internship at Harbourline Media, I worked on its React news site, fixing accessibility issues across more than 20 components and building a reusable, keyboard- and screen-reader-friendly image gallery documented in Storybook. I also wrote unit tests with Jest and React Testing Library. For my final-year project, Tidewatch, I developed an accessible React and TypeScript app and a Node.js/Express API backed by PostgreSQL. I tested the app with NVDA and VoiceOver and achieved a Lighthouse accessibility score of 100. More recently, I built a booking website for a local yoga studio using Next.js and React.

Verdane Care’s focus on patients, privacy by default and accessible design particularly resonates with the care I take to make interfaces usable for people with different access needs. I would welcome the opportunity to bring my frontend and project-based full-stack experience to your patient-facing products and continue developing as an engineer on your team.

Thank you for considering my application. I would be glad to discuss how my experience could contribute to Verdane Care.

Yours sincerely,
Aiyana Brooks-Tan

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, concise cover letter with a professional tone and clear evidence from the Harbourline Media internship and Tidewatch project. It demonstrates React, TypeScript, Node.js, Express, PostgreSQL, accessibility, Storybook, Jest and React Testing Library through specific examples rather than unsupported claims. The progression from professional experience to academic full-stack work is easy to follow, and the connection to patient-facing, accessible products is relevant. It could be slightly more complete by explicitly identifying the candidate's degree status and Git-based workflow, and by making the motivation for Verdane Care more specific without adding generic enthusiasm.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The letter is ATS-friendly: it uses standard headings-free prose, normal punctuation, readable paragraphs and several exact job-description terms, including React, TypeScript, Node.js, Express, PostgreSQL, accessibility, Storybook, Jest and React Testing Library. AI screening probability is high for the skills actually evidenced in the candidate material, but lower for the full must-have profile because the letter does not mention Git/GitHub, HTML/CSS foundations or fluent English, and the candidate material does not support automated end-to-end testing, OWASP/security knowledge or two years of professional experience. Do not add unsupported terms such as NestJS, Playwright, OWASP, GDPR expertise or health-data experience.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The letter aligns well with Verdane Care's patient-facing focus, accessible design principles and frontend/full-stack scope. The candidate's accessibility work is particularly relevant to the role, and the yoga-studio booking project provides a truthful wellness-related connection. However, the candidate's material shows less than two years of professional web-application experience, no demonstrated end-to-end testing, no documented OWASP/security awareness, and no healthcare or regulated-environment experience. These are candidate-profile gaps rather than defects in the letter. The letter also does not explicitly show the candidate's Git-based workflow or native English, although both are present in the candidate material and can be added accurately.
critique.improvement_instructions:
MINOR, ATS-RELEVANT ENHANCEMENTS:
1. In the second paragraph, after “I also wrote unit tests with Jest and React Testing Library,” add a truthful sentence showing the supported version-control requirement: “I use Git and GitHub in my development work.” Do not describe this as a team workflow or claim a specific branching/review process, because that is not documented in the candidate information.
2. In the opening paragraph, after the first sentence, add the candidate's qualification to establish context: “I recently completed a BSc (Hons) in Computing – Software Development at Liffey Institute of Technology, graduating with First Class Honours.” This is supported by the CV and makes the early-career level clear.
3. In the final body paragraph, replace “continue developing as an engineer on your team” with a more role-specific but still accurate closing such as “contribute my React accessibility experience and project-based Node.js/PostgreSQL work to your patient-facing products while continuing to grow as a full-stack engineer.” This preserves the truthful distinction between professional frontend experience and project-based backend experience.
4. Do not add claims about two years of professional experience, end-to-end testing, Playwright, NestJS, OWASP, GDPR, health-data privacy experience, AWS, Docker or healthcare software; none is supported by the Original Candidate Information.

critique.content_quality_feedback: The cover letter is concise, professional, and logically structured. It provides credible evidence for the strongest matches: React accessibility work, TypeScript, Node.js/Express, PostgreSQL, automated unit testing, Storybook, and Git/GitHub. The Tidewatch and Harbourline examples are specific and persuasive. However, the final paragraph repeats “patient-facing products,” and the letter could connect the yoga booking project more directly to the role’s wellness context. It also does not clearly distinguish the candidate’s professional experience from project-based experience, although it appropriately avoids claiming the required two years.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The letter uses several valuable job-description terms, including React, TypeScript, Node.js, Express, PostgreSQL, accessibility, Storybook, Jest, React Testing Library, Git, and GitHub. Its plain text structure is ATS-friendly, with no tables, graphics, headers, or unusual formatting. AI screening probability is moderate to good when read alongside the CV, but the cover letter itself omits Next.js, despite this being a relevant nice-to-have, and does not mention semantic HTML, responsive layouts, end-to-end testing, web security, or privacy requirements. Those omissions should not be filled with unsupported claims. The repeated wording in the closing paragraph is a minor professionalism issue.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The letter aligns well with the role’s patient-facing and accessibility focus. The Tidewatch project demonstrates full-stack project experience with React, TypeScript, Node.js/Express, PostgreSQL, screen-reader testing, and strong accessibility results. The yoga-studio booking site provides relevant wellness-domain context, and the Harbourline internship supports the role’s testing and Storybook requirements. The candidate has genuine gaps against the stated 2+ years of professional React/TypeScript experience, end-to-end testing, explicit web-security fundamentals, health-data privacy experience or stated willingness to learn it, AWS/Docker, and analytics/A/B testing. These are candidate-experience gaps rather than defects that can be fixed through wording. German or Croatian is also not evidenced, while fluent English is demonstrated by the letter and listed as native English in the candidate information.
critique.improvement_instructions:
MINOR CONTENT AND PRECISION IMPROVEMENTS:
1. In the paragraph beginning “During my Software Development internship,” revise the final sentence about the yoga project to include the supported Next.js and deployment details: change “More recently, I built a booking website for a local yoga studio using Next.js and React.” to “More recently, I built and deployed a booking website for a local yoga studio using Next.js, React and Tailwind CSS.” This adds a relevant job keyword and makes the wellness connection more concrete without overstating the work.
2. In the third paragraph, remove the duplicated phrase “to your patient-facing products.” For example, replace the full sentence beginning “I would welcome the opportunity” with: “I would welcome the opportunity to bring my frontend and project-based full-stack experience to Verdane Care’s patient-facing products while continuing to grow as a full-stack engineer.”
3. In the third paragraph, make the company-principle connection more specific while retaining only supported claims. Replace “the care I take to make interfaces usable for people with different access needs” with “my experience improving keyboard navigation, colour contrast, ARIA labels and screen-reader usability.” This ties the motivation paragraph directly to evidence already described earlier in the letter.
4. In the opening paragraph, clarify the scope of experience rather than allowing “my experience” to imply two years of professional work. Change “My experience building accessible React interfaces, alongside project-based work with TypeScript, Node.js, Express and PostgreSQL” to “My internship experience building accessible React interfaces, alongside project-based full-stack work with TypeScript, Node.js, Express and PostgreSQL.”
